rules.title: Newark rent control: annual rent increase cap
rules.requirement: If your Newark apartment is rent-controlled, your rent cannot go up more than the allowed percentage in any 12-month period, and never more than 4%, even if the unit changes tenants or owners. No increase is allowed if the building is not in substantial code compliance or the landlord has not registered the unit.
rules.key_value: never more than 4% in any consecutive 12-month period

coverage.summary: Residential rental units subject to Newark's Rent Control Ordinance (Title 19, Chapter 2). The page says only 'certain residential rental units' and does not state the unit-count, construction-date or other exemptions. Commercial space is not covered.

rules.exemptions: Not stated on this page beyond 'certain residential rental units'; increases are barred where the dwelling is not in substantial compliance or the landlord has not met registration requirements (§ 19:2-9.8).
rules.penalty: The annual increase is not permitted if the dwelling is not in substantial compliance or the landlord has not registered.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%. The allowable annual increase will not be permitted, if the dwelling is not in substantial compliance and/or if the landlord has not met the registration requirements as specified in this subsection 19:2-9.8.
rules.interaction: The section's text is cited to the amendment Ord. 6 PSF-A(S), adopted 2017-09-05. Under N.J.S.A. 40:69A-181(b) that amendment would take effect 20 days after final passage (about 2017-09-25), but the page does not say whether the 4% ceiling began with that amendment, so the effective date is left null. A 2020 executive order (MEO-20-0004) froze increases on rent-controlled units; it was rescinded on 2023-09-18, with 0% applying for the moratorium period.

notes: This is an official Newark city page that quotes Mun. Code 19:2-3.1. Coverage details (which units are rent-controlled) are not stated. The 1.3% figure is a January 2015 example only and was not used as the current figure. The 2020 rent-increase moratorium (Executive Order MEO-20-0004) was rescinded on 2023-09-18 and is not recorded as a separate rule. The page mentions retaliation and discrimination only as matters outside the Board's jurisdiction, so no rule was extracted for them.
